text: On 24 May 2023 the user said they had been taking a Coursera course on data science and machine learning and wanted supplementary books to deepen their learning.

The assistant recommended foundational data science and machine learning books: 'Python Machine Learning' by Sebastian Raschka, 'Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow' by Aurélien Géron, and 'Data Science for Dummies' by Lillian Pierson.

The assistant recommended math and statistics books: 'Linear Algebra and Its Applications' by Gilbert Strang, 'Probability and Statistics for Data Science' by Jim Henley, and 'Calculus for Data Science' by Stefan Waner and Steven R. Costenoble.

The assistant recommended deep learning books 'Deep Learning' by Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio and Aaron Courville, and 'Deep Learning with Python' by François Chollet, plus specialised books 'Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning' by Christopher Bishop, 'Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction' by Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, and 'Natural Language Processing (almost) from Scratch' by Collobert et al.

The assistant also recommended career-oriented books: 'Data Science Handbook' by Jake VanderPlas on becoming a data scientist, and 'Building Data Science Teams' by DJ Patil on building and managing data science teams.
The user, a beginner, asked for more details on 'Data Science for Dummies' after hearing it is a great resource for beginners like them.

The assistant said 'Data Science for Dummies' was written by Lillian Pierson for readers with little or no prior experience, including non-technical readers and business professionals, and that it uses minimal math and jargon.

The assistant described 'Data Science for Dummies' as having six parts: data science fundamentals, data preparation, data analysis, machine learning, big data and advanced analytics, and data science in practice. It includes exercises, quizzes and a glossary.

The assistant gave pros of 'Data Science for Dummies' as a friendly writing style and coverage of the whole data science process, and cons as being unsuitable for advanced data scientists and possibly too casual for some readers.
On 24 May 2023 the user said they would buy 'Data Science for Dummies' and asked for online resources to learn linear algebra.

The assistant recommended linear algebra resources including Khan Academy's Linear Algebra Course, MIT OpenCourseWare's Linear Algebra materials, Gilbert Strang's free online textbook, 3Blue1Brown's Linear Algebra series, and Coursera's four-course Linear Algebra Specialization from the University of Pennsylvania.

The assistant also listed edX's 12-week Linear Algebra and Matrix Theory course from UC Berkeley, Udemy's Linear Algebra for Machine Learning course, Gilbert Strang's YouTube lecture playlist, and Khan Academy and MIT practice problems.

The user said they would start with Khan Academy's Linear Algebra Course and then move on to Coursera's Linear Algebra Specialization, and asked for resources to supplement their Duolingo study of Spanish.
The assistant recommended Spanish learning platforms SpanishDict, Babbel and Rosetta Stone, plus flashcard and vocabulary apps Anki, Memrise and Quizlet.

The assistant recommended Spanish courses: Coursera's Spanish for Beginners, a 5-course specialization by Universidad Carlos III de Madrid, and edX's Spanish Language and Culture, a 4-course series by Universidad de Salamanca.
The assistant recommended Spanish podcasts Coffee Break Spanish, Spanish Obsessed and News in Slow Spanish, and language exchange options Conversation Exchange, Tandem and HelloTalk.

On 24 May 2023 the user said they would start with SpanishDict and then move on to Coursera's Spanish for Beginners course, and that they had completed 50 episodes of Crash Course's Science series, which had helped them understand the basics of science.

The assistant congratulated the user on completing 50 episodes of Crash Course Science, hosted by Hank Green and Sabrina Cruz, and suggested further Crash Course series: Chemistry and Biology (Hank Green), Physics (Shini Somara) and Astronomy (Phil Plait).
On 25 May 2023 the user said they had recently splurged on $800 boots, a tough lesson in overspending, and were cutting back on luxury shopping while still wanting to look great on a budget.

The assistant gave ten budget fashion tips, including shopping sales and clearance, high-street brands such as H&M, Zara, Uniqlo and ASOS, thrift and resale through ThredUp, Poshmark and eBay, and discount retailers TJ Maxx, Marshalls and Ross.

The assistant also suggested clothes swaps with friends, DIY upcycling, investing in timeless pieces such as a good pair of jeans or a leather jacket, and styling existing clothes. It told the user not to regret the $800 boots and to treat them as a lesson.
The user said they had never thought about renting clothes for special occasions and asked for recommendations of clothing rental services or websites.

The assistant recommended Rent the Runway (designer dresses, rentals of 4-8 days), Vestiare Collective (pre-owned luxury such as Chanel, Gucci and Louis Vuitton, rentals of 4-14 days) and The RealReal (designer pieces, rentals of 4-10 days).

The assistant also listed ThredUp Go (a box of 7-10 items for a flat fee), Le Tote (a monthly box of 3-5 items), Gwynnie Bee (a monthly plus-size subscription), Armarium (designer pieces, rentals of 4-10 days) and Nuuly (a monthly subscription).
On 25 May 2023 the user asked for budget-friendly fashion bloggers or influencers who share the user's budget-conscious mindset and could provide affordable style inspiration.

The assistant recommended bloggers We Wore What (@weworewhat, Danielle Bernstein), The Budget Babe (@thebudgetbabe, Dianna Baros) and Frugal Fashionista (@frugalfashionista), plus YouTube creators NikkieTutorials, The Fashion Citizen and Fashionista Barbie.

The assistant also suggested TikTok creators @fashionbyally, @budgetfashionista and @thriftwithme, and Instagram accounts @budgetfashionista, @fashiononabudget and @thriftstorefashionista, for budget fashion content.
On 25 May 2023 the user asked for help finding boots similar to their recently purchased luxury boots at a lower price point.

The user's $800 boots were black ankle boots with a heel from a luxury brand. The user valued their sleek design, quality leather and the confidence and style they gave the user, and hoped to find something similar for much less.

The assistant suggested alternatives priced from $80 to $250: ASOS Design Ankle Boot ($80-100), Steve Madden Baily Boot ($100-150), Clarks Wave Boot ($150-180), and the Sam Edelman Hazel Boot and Vince Camuto Betina Boot (both about $200-250).
The assistant said an exact replica at a much lower price would be hard to find, and suggested buying gently used luxury boots from The RealReal, ThredUp or eBay as a way to get a lower price.
The user said they were not sure about spending $200-$250 on boots and were thinking more along the lines of $50-$100, asking for suggestions in that range.

The assistant suggested $50-$100 boot options: Old Navy ankle boots from about $30-$40, Target ankle boots from about $30-$50, Forever 21 ankle boots from about $20-$40, H&M ankle boots from about $30-$60, and Amazon ankle boots from about $30-$70.

The assistant named specific $50-$100 options: Amazon's Ollio Ankle Boot (about $40-$50), H&M's Ankle Boot with Heel (about $40-$50) and Forever 21's Ankle Boot with Block Heel (about $25-$35), and suggested shopping sales or using coupons for better deals.
On 21 May 2023 the user said they had recently bought boots they loved but thought they could have found something similar for much less.

On 21 May 2023 the user said a budget store had similar boots for $50, which made them rethink their spending habits, and asked for tips on avoiding impulse purchases and staying on track with budgeting.

The assistant recommended a 30-day waiting rule before buying non-essential items, keeping a wish list, tracking expenses, avoiding tempting stores, and asking mindful consumption questions such as whether the user already owns something similar.

The assistant also recommended the 50/30/20 budget rule (50% necessities, 30% discretionary spending, 20% saving and debt repayment), paying with cash, removing shopping apps or websites from devices, and sharing budget goals with a friend for accountability.
On 21 May 2023 the user said they used to be a luxury shopper, were scaling back, and asked for tips on finding affordable alternatives to luxury brands.

The assistant suggested finding luxury alternatives by listing the features the user loves, researching lower-priced brands, dupe hunting, and checking outlet stores for previous seasons' luxury-brand styles at lower prices.

The assistant listed affordable alternatives to luxury brands: Everlane for J.Crew or Madewell, Zara for Gucci or Prada, ASOS for Net-a-Porter or Farfetch, Sephora Collection for NARS or Tom Ford, and NYX for MAC or Urban Decay.

The assistant recommended high-street brands Madewell, Everlane and J.Crew Factory as better quality than fast fashion but cheaper than luxury, and suggested ThredUp, Poshmark and Depop for second-hand finds at a fraction of the original price.
On 21 May 2023 the user said they were thinking of buying a new pair of jeans and asked for tips on finding a pair that fits well and is affordable.

The assistant advised knowing waist size, inseam and leg shape before shopping for jeans, setting a budget anywhere from under $50 to over $200, and checking stitching, fabric quality, and zippers and rivets before buying.
The assistant suggested affordable jeans brands Old Navy, H&M, American Eagle, Levi's and Everlane, and noted that stretch denim is comfortable and suits most body types.
On 21 May 2023 the user said they had been looking at thrift stores and discount retailers for affordable options.

The assistant listed thrift stores Goodwill, Salvation Army, local charity shops, ThredUp and Poshmark, and discount retailers TJ Maxx, Marshalls, Ross, Burlington, Overstock and 6pm, and advised inspecting items for flaws and washing them before wearing.
The user said they had found a great pair of vintage jeans for $10 while thrift shopping and at discount retailers, and the assistant praised the find as a fantastic score.
On 20 May 2023 the user, who works in medical image analysis, asked for an overview of recent deep learning advances in the field and asked the assistant to skip the basics.

The assistant listed recent advances in deep learning for medical image analysis: multimodal fusion, self-supervised pretraining on unlabelled images, GAN and VAE image synthesis, attention and saliency explainability, transformers, 3D architectures, federated learning, and personalised medicine.

The assistant also noted advances in real-time analysis and integration with clinical workflows, and growing emphasis on regulatory standards, ethics, and bias and fairness in medical deep learning models.

On 20 May 2023 the user asked for popular datasets for training deep learning models on medical image segmentation tasks. The assistant recommended BRATS, with 750 MRI scans (T1, T2, FLAIR and T1ce), and MRBrainS, with 5 MRI scans of brain structures.

The assistant recommended cardiac segmentation datasets ACDC (150 cardiac MRI scans) and LVSC (30 cardiac MRI scans), and lung segmentation datasets LUNA (888 CT scans with lung nodule segmentations) and LOLA11 (55 lung CT scans).

The assistant recommended abdominal segmentation datasets CHAOS (40 abdominal CT scans) and BTCV (50 abdominal CT scans), plus general datasets MedMNIST, the Medical Segmentation Decathlon (MSD, 10 tasks), ISBI challenges and MICCAI Grand Challenges, and advised checking terms of use and licences.
On 20 May 2023 the user asked for the latest trends and advancements in explainable AI for medical image analysis.

The assistant listed explainable AI trends for medical imaging: attention-based models, gradient-based methods such as Grad-CAM and Guided Backpropagation, heatmaps, LIME, SHAP and TreeExplainer, explainable U-Net designs, and hybrid approaches combining several XAI techniques.

The assistant named explainable AI challenges for medical imaging: the interpretability versus accuracy trade-off, clinical validation, scalability and deployability, and explanations that non-experts such as clinicians without AI backgrounds can understand.

On 20 May 2023 the user asked for relevant research papers or articles on explainable AI in medical image analysis. The assistant recommended surveys by Rajpurkar et al. (2020), 'Explainable AI in Medical Imaging: A Survey', and Jimenez-Sánchez et al. (2020), 'Explanation Methods for Medical Image Analysis: A Systematic Review'.

The assistant recommended technical XAI papers: Selvaraju et al. (2017) on Grad-CAM, Schlemper et al. (2019) on attention-gated networks for ultrasound segmentation, Shrikumar et al. (2017) on DeepLIFT, and Zeiler and Fergus (2014) on visualizing and understanding CNNs.

The assistant recommended XAI application papers: Rajpurkar et al. (2020) on breast cancer diagnosis from mammography, Wang et al. (2020) on interpretable cardiac image segmentation, Chen et al. (2020) on lung nodule detection in CT scans, and review articles by Topol (2020) and Liu et al. (2020).

On 20 May 2023 the user asked for advanced papers on multi-modal image fusion, transfer learning and domain adaptation. The assistant recommended Wang et al. (2019), Rajpurkar et al. (2020) and Chen et al. (2020) on multi-modal fusion, including fusion for breast cancer diagnosis.

The assistant recommended transfer learning and domain adaptation papers: Shen et al. (2017) survey, Rajpurkar et al. (2020) transfer learning review, Wang et al. (2019) on brain tumour segmentation, Dou et al. (2020) domain adaptation survey, Chen et al. (2020) on cardiac segmentation, and Zhang et al. (2020) on adversarial domain adaptation for lung nodule detection.

The assistant recommended other advanced topic papers: Shen et al. (2020) survey on deep learning for medical image registration, Wang et al. (2020) review of GAN-based medical image synthesis, and Rajpurkar et al. (2020) review of explainable AI for medical image analysis.

The user asked for papers on visualizing and interpreting deep learning models in medical image analysis. The assistant recommended Zeiler and Fergus (2014), Yosinski et al. (2015) on deep visualization, Wang et al. (2019) on visualizing deep networks for medical image analysis, and Simonyan et al. (2014) on saliency maps.

The assistant recommended further interpretation papers: Chen et al. (2020) on attention-based saliency maps for breast cancer diagnosis, Wang et al. (2020) on visualizing attention, Zhang et al. (2020) survey on model interpretability techniques, and the LIME (Ribeiro et al., 2016) and SHAP (Lundberg and Lee, 2017) papers.

On 17 Nov 2022 the user was planning a Miami trip and wanted to redeem Delta SkyMiles for a free trip. They had just returned from a red-eye JetBlue flight from San Francisco to Boston and slept for almost the entire flight.
On 17 Nov 2022 the user said they had 10,000 SkyMiles and wanted a round-trip economy ticket from Boston to Miami. They were flexible on dates, preferred summer travel, and wanted a non-stop flight.

The assistant listed non-stop Delta Boston (BOS) to Miami (MIA) summer redemptions: June 15-22 at 9,500 miles, June 22-29 at 10,000, July 6-13 at 10,000, July 13-20 at 10,500, August 3-10 at 10,000, and August 10-17 at 10,500, subject to availability.

The assistant suggested checking Delta's website or app, setting price alerts, using ExpertFlyer to monitor availability, and noted that connecting flights might offer more options or lower redemption rates.

The assistant suggested considering Fort Lauderdale (FLL) as an alternative airport that might offer more redemption options or lower mileage requirements, and advised booking early and checking fees and change policies before redeeming.
On 17 Nov 2022 the user said they were considering applying for the Citi AAdvantage Executive credit card to earn more miles for future trips, and asked about its benefits and requirements.

The assistant said the Citi AAdvantage Executive card offers 50,000 AAdvantage miles after $5,000 spend in the first 3 months, 2x miles on American Airlines purchases, and 1x mile on all other purchases.

The assistant said the Citi AAdvantage Executive card has a $450 annual fee, typically requires a credit score of 700+ FICO, has no foreign transaction fee, and gives 10,000 anniversary miles after $40,000 spend in the previous year.

The assistant listed Citi AAdvantage Executive perks: Admirals Club access for the holder and up to 2 guests, priority check-in, security and boarding on American flights, a $100 Global Entry or TSA PreCheck fee credit, and 25% off in-flight food, beverages and headsets.
On 17 Nov 2022 the user said they were flying Spirit Airlines to Fort Lauderdale for a spring break trip in March and asked about Spirit's baggage policies and restrictions.

The assistant said Spirit includes one free personal item that must fit under the seat, that carry-on bags cost extra up to 22 x 14 x 9 inches, and estimated carry-on fees of $30-45 online and $40-55 at the airport.

The assistant said Spirit checked bags have a maximum size of 62 linear inches and a 40 lb weight limit, with estimated checked bag fees of $25-40 online and $35-50 at the airport, and overweight bag fees of $75-100.

On 17 Nov 2022 the user asked for affordable accommodation in Miami. The assistant recommended Jazz Hostel and Miami Beach Hostel, with dorms and private rooms from about $30-40 per night, plus Red Roof Inn Miami Airport ($60-80) and Super 8 by Wyndham Miami ($70-90).

The assistant recommended mid-range Miami options: Hampton Inn & Suites Miami Midtown ($100-120), Hyatt Place Miami Airport East ($120-140), Airbnb private rooms or apartments ($80-120), and VRBO rentals ($100-150).

The assistant's budget accommodation tips were to book early, stay flexible on dates, consider the May-September off-season for lower rates, compare Expedia, Booking.com and Hotels.com, and read reviews on TripAdvisor, Yelp or Google.

On 15 Jan 2023 the user said they had just earned 10,000 Delta SkyMiles on their Delta SkyMiles card after a round-trip Boston to Atlanta flight that day, and wanted to use them for a free trip to Miami later that year.
The assistant estimated that one-way economy flights within the continental United States typically need 5,000-10,000 miles, and round-trip economy flights need 10,000-20,000 miles.

The assistant advised using Delta's award calendar under 'Shop with Miles', flying on off-peak days such as Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Saturdays, travelling in mid-January to mid-March, and setting price alerts with ExpertFlyer or Google Flights.

On 15 Jan 2023 the user said they were flexible on travel dates and asked whether they could use SkyMiles on American Airlines, citing a poor in-flight entertainment experience on an American flight from New York to Los Angeles on February 10th.

The assistant said Delta and American Airlines are not airline partners, so Delta SkyMiles cannot be redeemed on American flights. Delta's partners named were LATAM, Air France, KLM and Virgin Atlantic.

On 15 Jan 2023 the user said they had recently been approved for the Citi AAdvantage Executive card, with a 50,000-mile bonus after $5,000 spend in 3 months, and asked whether to focus on American Airlines miles or diversify across airlines.

The assistant said American Airlines is part of the Oneworld alliance with British Airways, Cathay Pacific and Qantas, and that transferable points such as Chase Ultimate Rewards and Amex Membership Rewards can move to multiple airline loyalty programs.

On 15 Jan 2023 the user said they were considering the Chase Sapphire Preferred to diversify their miles, having heard that Chase Ultimate Rewards points are highly valued and transferable to multiple airline partners.

The assistant said the Chase Sapphire Preferred offers 60,000 bonus points after $4,000 spend in 3 months, 2X points on travel and dining, a 25% points bonus for travel redeemed through Chase Ultimate Rewards, and no foreign transaction fees.

The assistant suggested other cards: Chase Sapphire Reserve ($300 travel credit, lounge access), Amex Platinum (5X on flights booked directly or through Amex Travel, $200 airline fee credit), Citi Premier (3X on travel) and Capital One Venture (2X on all purchases).
The assistant suggested United MileagePlus, Delta SkyMiles and Hilton Honors as loyalty programs to consider for diversifying miles.
On 15 Jan 2023 the user asked how the Chase Ultimate Rewards portal works for redeeming points on travel bookings, and what travel insurance and assistance the Chase Sapphire Preferred offers.

The assistant said Ultimate Rewards points are worth 1.25 cents each when redeemed for travel with the 25% bonus, so 60,000 points could cover a $750 flight, and listed trip cancellation or interruption cover of up to $10,000 per person and $20,000 per trip.

The assistant said the Chase Sapphire Preferred also offers travel delay reimbursement of up to $500 per ticket for delays of 12 hours or more, trip delay reimbursement of up to $500 for delays of 6 hours or more, 24/7 travel assistance, and purchase and return protection.

On 28 Jan 2023 the user was planning a Miami trip and comparing American Airlines and Delta in-flight entertainment. They had a terrible experience with American's entertainment system on a New York to Los Angeles flight but said they would give American another chance.

On 28 Jan 2023 the user reported a 1-hour delay on their United Airlines flight from Boston to Chicago that day, caused by air traffic control issues, and said the pilot kept passengers well informed throughout the delay.

The assistant said American offers seat-back screens on most aircraft, including the Boeing 737-800, 777-200 and Airbus A321T, plus streaming to personal devices through its app with a wide selection of movies, TV, music and games.

The assistant said Delta offers Delta Studio on seat-back screens or through the Fly Delta app, with a content library often praised as more extensive and partner content from HBO and Showtime, and suggested the user might try Delta given their earlier American experience.

On 28 Jan 2023 the user asked for hotels near Miami airport that are within walking distance or offer a shuttle. The assistant named Miami International Airport Hotel, inside the airport, and Hyatt Regency Miami Airport, connected by skybridge.

The assistant listed Miami airport hotels with shuttles: Hilton Miami Airport Blue Lagoon (complimentary shuttle every 15-20 minutes, about a 5-minute drive), and Crowne Plaza Miami Airport and Fairfield Inn & Suites by Marriott Miami Airport South (shuttles about every 30 minutes, about a 10-minute drive).

The assistant also listed La Quinta Inn & Suites by Wyndham Miami Airport East and Embassy Suites by Hilton Miami International Airport, with shuttles about every 30 minutes, and Sheraton Miami Airport Hotel & Executive Meeting Center and DoubleTree by Hilton Miami Airport, which charge a shuttle fee.
On 28 Jan 2023 the user asked about Spirit Airlines' strict baggage rules before a planned trip to Fort Lauderdale, so they could prepare.

The assistant said Spirit's free personal item must fit under the seat with a maximum size of 18 x 14 x 8 inches, and that a carry-on up to 22 x 14 x 9 inches costs $35-45 online up to 24 hours before the flight, $45 during online check-in, and $55 at the airport.

The assistant said Spirit's first checked bag costs $30-40 online and $55 at the airport, additional checked bags cost $40-50 each, and overweight bags cost $30 for 41-50 lb, $75 for 51-70 lb and $100 for 71-100 lb.

The user planned a round-trip Boston to Fort Lauderdale ticket for March spring break and asked for the maximum personal item size on Spirit. The assistant answered 18 x 14 x 8 inches (45.7 x 35.5 x 20.3 cm).

On 28 Jan 2023 the user wanted a hotel near Miami airport with a free shuttle to the Port of Miami cruise terminal, for a cruise after the Miami trip. The assistant named Hyatt Regency Miami Airport, Hilton Miami Airport Blue Lagoon, Embassy Suites, Crowne Plaza Miami Airport and La Quinta as having such shuttles.
On 28 Jan 2023 the user said they were considering a room at Hyatt Regency Miami Airport and asked about the schedule of its cruise shuttle to the Port of Miami and how to reserve a spot.

The assistant said the Hyatt Regency Miami Airport cruise shuttle runs on cruise departure days with departures around 10:00 AM, 11:00 AM and 12:00 PM (subject to change), and a travel time of about 20-30 minutes depending on traffic.

The assistant said to reserve a Hyatt shuttle spot, the user should call the concierge at (305) 871-1234 with the cruise line, ship name and departure date, since shuttle spots are first-come, first-served and limited.

The assistant advised arriving at the hotel at least one day before cruise departure, reconfirming the shuttle a day or two before sailing, and arranging a private transfer or taxi if the user has a lot of luggage, since the shuttle has limited luggage space.
